title: For a proper geometrically normal scheme: trivial global functions, geometric connectedness, irreducibility and integrality are equivalent
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a proper geometrically normal scheme X over k, the lemma proves the equivalence of H^0(X, O_X) = k, geometric connectedness, geometric irreducibility and geometric integrality (statement lines 2269-2279). The proof takes the four implications in turn: the equivalence of the first two is the geometrically reduced Stein statement proved just before; the equivalence of connectedness and irreducibility uses that a locally Noetherian normal scheme is a disjoint union of its irreducible components, applied to the base change to the algebraic closure; and the equivalence with integrality uses that the base change is reduced, so irreducibility gives integrality (proof lines 2281-2289). The claim is H2: three cited inputs, each doing exactly one equivalence, with the passage to the base change over the algebraic closure as the common thread.
